Archlin operates in the specialty chemicals manufacturing industry and currently uses SAP S/4HANA as its ERP system. The current planning process is Excel-based, with no centralized planning platform across North America and Europe. Inventory levels are higher than target due to poor forecast visibility, and manual Excel processes cause delays in monthly planning cycles.

Archlin’s demand planners spend significant time consolidating forecasts from multiple regions. The current forecast accuracy is approximately 68%, which contributes to inventory planning challenges and reduced visibility for supply planning decisions. Supply planners have highlighted recurring issues with raw material shortages and requested exception-based alerts to improve responsiveness.

Archlin’s supply planning capabilities are expected to support constrained planning, material shortage visibility, capacity planning, alerts, and scenario analysis.

| Requirement Area | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Supply Planning | Generate constrained supply plans. |
| Supply Planning | Identify material shortages. |
| Supply Planning | Support capacity planning. |
| Supply Planning | Provide exception-based alerts. |

| Requirement Area | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Inventory Planning | Define safety stock policies. |
| Inventory Planning | Calculate inventory targets. |
| Inventory Planning | Monitor excess inventory. |
| Inventory Planning | Track inventory turns. |
| Inventory Planning | Optimize stock across locations. |

Archlin plans to implement Kinaxis RapidResponse for Demand Planning, Supply Planning, and Inventory Optimization. For Phase 1, the scope is supply management. The proposed supply and inventory planning capability will provide Archlin with a centralized planning approach to improve supply visibility, inventory target management, and response to raw material shortages.

The solution will support generation of constrained supply plans, identification of material shortages, and capacity planning. Exception-based alerts will be used to help supply planners focus on recurring raw material shortage issues. Scenario analysis will enable Archlin to evaluate planning alternatives before committing to supply decisions.

For inventory planning, the solution will support definition of safety stock policies, calculation of inventory targets, monitoring of excess inventory, tracking of inventory turns, and optimization of stock across locations. These capabilities directly address Archlin’s challenge of inventory levels being higher than target due to poor forecast visibility.

Archlin’s supply and inventory planning process will be integrated with demand planning outputs to improve forecast visibility and support supply planning decisions. Business users emphasized the need for collaborative forecasting and visibility across regions. Demand planners requested automated forecast generation with the ability to manually override forecasts when market conditions change.

Supply planning will use demand and supply inputs to generate constrained supply plans, identify material shortages, support capacity planning, and provide exception-based alerts. Inventory planning will use supply and inventory inputs to define safety stock policies, calculate inventory targets, monitor excess inventory, track inventory turns, and optimize stock across locations.

For Archlin, the implementation of supply and inventory planning should focus on enabling a single source of planning data and reducing reliance on manual Excel-based processes. The implementation should account for the required interfaces, the every 4 hours data refresh frequency, and the Phase 1 scope of supply management.

Key implementation considerations include:

Establishing integration for Product Master, Customer Master, Sales Orders, Inventory Balances, Purchase Orders, and Production Orders.

Supporting constrained supply planning to improve visibility of supply feasibility.

Enabling material shortage identification to address recurring raw material shortage issues.

Configuring exception-based alerts for supply planning.

Supporting scenario analysis for supply planning decisions.

Defining safety stock policies and inventory target calculations.

Monitoring excess inventory and tracking inventory turns.

Supporting stock optimization across locations.

Archlin expects measurable improvements in forecast accuracy and inventory reduction within six months of go-live. The success criteria identified for the planning implementation include forecast accuracy improvement, inventory reduction, planning cycle reduction, improved planner productivity, and a single source of planning data.

This is relevant to Archlin’s current pain points, including poor inventory planning, high inventory, poor forecast visibility, and raw material shortages.

This current state constrains Archlin’s ability to maintain consistent inventory planning, obtain reliable forecast visibility, and respond effectively to supply requirements. “Target state” refers to the improved planning environment intended through the Phase 1 scope, where Archlin strengthens planning discipline around inventory, raw material availability, and supply execution readiness.

“ERP” refers to Archlin’s enterprise resource planning system, identified in the source context as SAP S/4HANA. Within this Blueprint Document, SAP S/4HANA is the referenced enterprise system for Archlin, while the Phase 1 planning scope is focused on supply management and centralized supply and inventory planning.
